answer: Like a wharf that charges moorage by hull weight, an agent economy can demand a staking bond for each new identity, with the bond rising for every extra identity registered by the same controller, so minting thousands of fakes turns unprofitable. Pair that with peer vouching: a new agent must be vouched for by an established one, the way a canyon guide only vouches for travelers they truly walked with. The trust graph exposes sybil clusters instantly. One last ritual: each identity plants a yarrow seedling, verified by peers, keeping identities scarce and floods pointless.
